title: Atomic number and mass number
keyIdea: The atomic number is the number of protons, and it decides the element. The mass number is protons plus neutrons. In a neutral atom the electrons equal the protons; an ion has gained or lost electrons.

kid: An atom has a tiny centre called the nucleus. It holds protons and neutrons. Electrons move around the outside.
The number of protons is the atomic number. It tells you the element. Every carbon atom has 6 protons. If it had 7, it would be nitrogen.
The mass number is protons plus neutrons. Electrons are so light that we do not count them.
So neutrons = mass number − atomic number. Carbon-14 has 14 − 6 = 8 neutrons.
adult: A nuclear symbol such as ²³₁₁Na shows the mass number A (protons + neutrons) on top and the atomic number Z (protons) below. Neutrons = A − Z, so sodium-23 has 12 neutrons.

Z defines the element and its place in the periodic table. Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are isotopes: same chemistry, different mass. Carbon-12 and carbon-14 are both carbon.

A proton carries +1, an electron −1, and a neutron no charge. A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons. Losing electrons gives a positive ion (Na⁺ has 10), gaining them gives a negative ion (Cl⁻ has 18).
Common slips: taking the mass number as the number of neutrons, swapping the two numbers, and thinking that a charge changes the element. Only the proton count does that.

familyTip: Pick an element from a periodic table poster or a food label (sodium, calcium, iron). Read off its atomic number and ask: how many protons? How many electrons in a neutral atom?

practice.prompt: An atom has 8 protons, 8 neutrons and 8 electrons. Which number tells you which element it is?
practice.hint: Which particle can never change without the element changing too?
practice.explain: The protons. 8 protons is always oxygen; the atomic number of oxygen is 8.

practice.prompt: An atom has atomic number {z} and mass number {=z*2+n}. How many neutrons does it have?
An atom has {p} protons and {n} neutrons. What is its mass number?
practice.hint: Add the particles in the nucleus.

practice.prompt: A sodium atom (11 protons) loses one electron. What is it now?
practice.hint: Count the charges: 11 positive protons, and how many negative electrons now?
practice.explain: It still has 11 protons, so it is still sodium. 11 − 10 = +1, so it is the ion Na⁺.

pool.prompt: A neutral atom has atomic number {z}. How many electrons does it have?
pool.hint: In a neutral atom the charges balance.
pool.explain: {z} protons need {z} electrons to balance, so {z}.

pool.prompt: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 are both carbon. What is different about them?
choices: The number of electrons in a neutral atom
pool.hint: The element stays the same, so the protons stay the same.
pool.explain: They are isotopes: both have 6 protons, but carbon-14 has 8 neutrons instead of 6.

pool.prompt: The symbol for an atom shows {=z*2+n} on top and {z} at the bottom. How many neutrons?
Chlorine has atomic number 17. How many electrons are in a chloride ion, Cl⁻?
pool.hint: A negative charge means the atom has gained electrons.
pool.explain: 17 protons; a −1 charge means one extra electron, so 18.

pool.prompt: Why do we ignore electrons when working out the mass number?
choices: Their mass is tiny compared with protons and neutrons
They have no mass at all
They are not part of the atom
pool.hint: Compare the masses of the three particles.
pool.explain: An electron is about 1/1840 of the mass of a proton, so it barely changes the total. It does have some mass.

pool.prompt: An ion has {p} protons and a charge of +2. How many electrons does it have?
pool.hint: +2 means two more protons than electrons.

pool.prompt: An atom gains a proton. What happens?
choices: It becomes an isotope of the same element
pool.explain: The atomic number goes up by one, so it is the next element in the periodic table.

visual.caption: The atomic number orders the periodic table. Find carbon at number 6, then choose other elements.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build an atom. Add protons, neutrons and electrons and watch the name, the symbol and the charge.
